subject: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput baseline and next steps
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@clarityai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: sales@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 13:02:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput baseline and next steps

Hi Jonas,

Thanks — we signed up for a trial yesterday and saw promising latency numbers on the hosted flow. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated because we need predictable throughput and data isolation for a search+RAG feature. Quick context:
- Company: ClarityAI (NLP search product for internal client-facing portals)
- Peak concurrent QPS anticipated: ~200 QPS sustained during daily batch windows (short spikes up to ~300 for 5–10 minutes)
- Latency SLO: 150 ms p95 for 512-token sequences
- Typical prompt length: 250–400 tokens; responses average ~120 tokens
- Data residency: US region required

We'd like a technical walkthrough focused on Dedicated capacity sizing and a short proof-of-concept plan (how we validate throughput/latency in a week). Preferred time windows next week: mornings PT (9–11am PT) on June 11–13.

I've attached a tiny perf sample from our test harness (perf_sample.csv) to give a sense of request distribution.

Can you connect us with the right engineer and book a 45-minute walkthrough? Also, any prep materials you recommend?

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Platform
ClarityAI
attachments: perf_sample.csv (csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@clarityai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, sales@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 14:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity demo — throughput baseline and next steps

Hi Asha — great to meet you (virtually). Thanks for the perf sample — helpful context. We can absolutely run a Dedicated sizing walkthrough and propose a short POC plan. A few rapid clarifying questions so we make the session tactical:

- Is 200 QPS your steady-state or an expected peak during business hours?
- How bursty is traffic (do spikes tend to be sub-second, or multi-minute)?
- Are you planning to use a single model family for serving (e.g., Llama-variant / opt / other) or mix generations and rerank/embeddings?
- Do you need private connectivity (VPC) for the POC or are you ok with a temporary hosted endpoint under NDA?

Proposed times (PT):
- Tue June 11, 9:30–10:15am PT
- Wed June 12, 10:00–10:45am PT

If neither works, suggest a time and I'll adjust. I'll bring Ben (solutions engineer) to cover throughput testing and Karthik to speak to deployment options and autoscale behaviors. I've attached a short intake MAP (SDR-intake-MAP.pdf) and a one-page agenda — if you can share the answers to the questions above we'll tailor the demo to your needs.

High-level agenda (45 min):
1) 10 min — Clarity on workload and goals
2) 10 min — Dedicated architecture and capacity sizing approach
3) 15 min — Throughput testing plan and POC steps
4) 10 min — Next steps and timeline (POC acceptance criteria)

If it's helpful we'll run a short preliminary smoke test during the call with sample requests.

Jonas Weber
SDR, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0143
Redwood Inference
attachments: SDR-intake-MAP.pdf (pdf)

From: Asha Rao <asha@clarityai.com>

Thanks Jonas — Wed June 12, 10:00–10:45am PT works for us. Confirming a few details to save time on the call:

- 200 QPS is our target steady-state during the heavy window; spikes to ~300 are brief but real (3–8 minutes).
- Typical prompt lengths are 250–400 tokens; avg response ~120 tokens.
- We'll be using a single generative model for responses and a small reranker for top-k scoring — both should be included in the stress plan.
- We will need US data residency and VPC connectivity for production, but for the POC we can use a temporary secure hosted endpoint under NDA.

I've attached our SOC2 questionnaire and a short network diagram so you can confirm the networking options ahead of time (soc2_answers.xlsx). Also: are there any limits on concurrent KV cache size or prefix caching behavior we should be aware of?

See you Wednesday — please send a calendar invite and prep doc link.

—Asha

Perfect — confirmed for Wed June 12, 10:00–10:45am PT (calendar invite attached).

Ben will lead the throughput/benchmarking portion and bring a short test harness we can run together. Karthik will cover Dedicated autoscale and VPC/private deployment options. To prep, please review the short agenda and the prep folder (Drive link below) — I've included a checklist for the smoke test (token sizes, concurrency ramp, and example curl commands).

Quick answers to the network/cache questions:
- KV/prefix cache sizing is configurable for Dedicated; we'll propose starting defaults for your sequence lengths and adjust during the POC.
- For host-level concurrency we typically recommend concurrent worker configuration to match target QPS with room for headroom; Ben will propose an initial plan based on the perf sample.
